calls.reasoning: Last published FRED value is 3.48 (Nov 5), following the Nasdaq-100's 6.4% drop. HY OAS has widened from ~2.60 in late August to ~3.3-3.5 and is now in a volatile regime with daily moves of 5-15bp. Nov 6: S&P +0.3%, VIX fell 9% to 25.6, and the strong jobs report raised expectations of a December Fed hike. I center on a random walk from roughly 3.45, since a rebound tightening offsets the pressure from energy-sector weakness (energy -11% on the week) and the risk of a hike. I add a right skew because spreads widen faster than they tighten under stress, and put a ~3% tail above 4.255 for a credit blowout. No Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold market was found for HY OAS.

calls.reasoning: The latest FRED print is 3.48 for Nov 5. It is the high of a widening episode that began near 2.65 in mid-September and followed the Nov 5 chip/AI equity crash. On Nov 6 equities partly rebounded, the VIX fell, and HY ETFs were roughly flat to slightly lower. The strong jobs report raised Treasury yields, which tends to hold OAS flat or slightly tighter, so Nov 6 probably prints around 3.40-3.48. I treat the path to Nov 20 as a near-random walk from about 3.44, with a little mean reversion after spikes (as in October: 3.24 to 3.03, then 3.40 to 3.14). The regime is volatile, with an ~0.27pp SD over 10 days. Upside risks give a right skew: CCC spreads at 4-year highs, energy weakness, December Fed hike odds and continued AI-equity stress. I put ~3% on a break above 4.255. No Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market was found by the runs or by the harness.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual record (FRED path through Nov 5 = 3.48; Nov 6 not yet published; Nov 20 is the resolution date; no prediction market). The only factual differences are minor: the size of the Nov 5 Nasdaq drop (-5.5% for the composite vs -6.36% for the Nasdaq-100; these are probably different indices, so both can be right) and the Nov 6 HYG move (-0.06% vs ~-0.3%; the -0.3% figure most likely refers to Nov 5). Neither changes the center much, and I could not verify either without web access. The judgment calls were mean reversion vs momentum and the size of the tail. Like the runs, I take a median slightly below the last print, because of how October's spikes partly reversed and because the Nov 6 macro/ETF tone was calm. I keep the runs' ~0.68 width and right skew, which I agree is consistent with realized volatility. I place the upper escape at 3%, since a +78bp move in two weeks needs an Apr-2025-type shock and the current backdrop of CCC stress and equity turmoil makes that non-negligible.
